var NOTES = "<h2>What Is Science?</h2>" + "<p>Science is the systematic study of the natural world through observation, experimentation, and reasoning. Scientists ask questions, form hypotheses, collect data, and draw conclusions based on evidence \u2014 not opinions or guesses.</p>" + "<p>The three main branches of science:</p>" + "<ul><li><strong>Life Science</strong> \u2014 the study of living things (biology)</li><li><strong>Physical Science</strong> \u2014 the study of matter and energy (chemistry + physics)</li><li><strong>Earth Science</strong> \u2014 the study of Earth and space (geology, meteorology, astronomy)</li></ul>" + "<h2>The Scientific Method</h2>" + "<p>The scientific method is a step-by-step process scientists use to investigate questions. The steps are not always linear \u2014 scientists often loop back and revise.</p>" + "<ol><li><strong>Ask a Question</strong> \u2014 What do you want to know?</li><li><strong>Research</strong> \u2014 What do you already know? What have others discovered?</li><li><strong>Form a Hypothesis</strong> \u2014 A testable prediction. <code>If\u2026 then\u2026 because\u2026</code></li><li><strong>Experiment</strong> \u2014 Design a controlled test.</li><li><strong>Collect Data</strong> \u2014 Record observations and measurements.</li><li><strong>Analyze Data</strong> \u2014 Look for patterns, calculate averages, make graphs.</li><li><strong>Draw Conclusions</strong> \u2014 Was your hypothesis supported or not?</li><li><strong>Communicate Results</strong> \u2014 Share findings with others.</li></ol>" + "<h2>Variables and Controls</h2>" + "<p>Every good experiment has three types of variables:</p>" + "<ul><li><strong>Independent Variable (IV)</strong> \u2014 The one thing you change on purpose.</li><li><strong>Dependent Variable (DV)</strong> \u2014 The thing you measure; it depends on the IV.</li><li><strong>Control Variables (Constants)</strong> \u2014 Everything that stays the same.</li></ul>" + "<p><strong>Control Group:</strong> The group that does not receive the experimental treatment. Used for comparison. Example: A plant given no fertilizer while others get fertilizer.</p>" + "<p><strong>Experimental Group:</strong> The group that receives the treatment.</p>" + "<h2>Data and Graphing</h2>" + "<p>Data comes in two flavors:</p>" + "<ul><li><strong>Qualitative Data</strong> \u2014 Descriptions. Uses your senses. (\"The liquid turned cloudy.\")</li><li><strong>Quantitative Data</strong> \u2014 Numbers. Measurements. (\"The liquid reached 45\u00b0C.\")</li></ul>" + "<p>Types of graphs:</p>" + "<ul><li><strong>Bar Graph</strong> \u2014 Comparing categories.</li><li><strong>Line Graph</strong> \u2014 Showing change over time.</li><li><strong>Pie Chart</strong> \u2014 Showing parts of a whole.</li></ul>" + "<p>Rules for graphing: label both axes with units, give the graph a title like <code>The Effect of [IV] on [DV]</code>, use a ruler. Neatness counts.</p>" + "<h2>Example \u2014 Why Bread Gets Soggy</h2>" + "<bq><strong>Question:</strong> Why does my sandwich bread get soggy when I put sauce on it?<br/><br/><strong>Background research:</strong> Bread is porous \u2014 it has tiny holes. Sauce has water in it. Water moves from wet things to dry things through a process called diffusion. The bread soaks up the water from the sauce. This is why the bread gets soggy.<br/><br/><strong>Hypothesis:</strong> If I put sauce on bread and wait, then the bread will get soggy because the water in the sauce soaks into the bread.<br/><br/><strong>Experiment:</strong> Take 3 slices of the same bread. Slice 1 gets no sauce (control). Slice 2 gets 1 tablespoon of sauce. Slice 3 gets 3 tablespoons of sauce. Wait 10 minutes. Measure how soggy each slice is by pressing a paper towel on it and seeing how much water comes off.<br/><br/><strong>Data:</strong> Slice 1 \u2014 paper towel dry. Slice 2 \u2014 small wet spot. Slice 3 \u2014 big wet spot, bread falling apart.<br/><br/><strong>Conclusion:</strong> The hypothesis was supported. More sauce = more sogginess. The water in the sauce soaks into the bread.<br/><br/><strong>Real-world fix:</strong> Put a layer of something between the sauce and the bread \u2014 like lettuce, cheese, or butter. Butter is fat and fat blocks water. This is why people butter their bread before making a sandwich.</bq>" + "<h2>Vocabulary Review</h2>" + "<table><tr><th>Term</th><th>Definition</th></tr>" + "<tr><td>Science</td><td>The systematic study of the natural world</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Hypothesis</td><td>A testable prediction based on observations</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Independent Variable</td><td>The variable the scientist changes on purpose</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Dependent Variable</td><td>The variable that is measured</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Control Group</td><td>The group that receives no experimental treatment</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Constant</td><td>A factor that stays the same in an experiment</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Data</td><td>Information collected during an experiment</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Qualitative Data</td><td>Descriptive observations using the senses</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Quantitative Data</td><td>Numerical measurements</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Inference</td><td>A logical conclusion based on evidence</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Observation</td><td>Information gathered using the five senses</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Theory</td><td>A well-tested explanation supported by much evidence</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Law</td><td>A rule describing a pattern in nature</td></tr>" + "<tr><td>Model</td><td>A representation used to explain something</td></tr>" + "</table>" + "<p style='margin-top:26px;font-style:italic;color:var(--mut);font-size:13px'>End of Chapter 1 notes. Additional reference material available via the button in the corner.</p>";
